_comment: The clean pz-only MATBLG transport calculation of P. Alcazar Guerrero et al., Phys. Rev. Lett. 134, 126301 (2025). One pz orbital per carbon, Slater-Koster pp_pi / pp_sigma channels with the paper's distance dependence, a 16x16x1 tiling of the relaxed moire unit cell, sampled at Gamma. THE ONE THING YOU MUST SUPPLY is structure.file: the relaxed moire unit cell, in POSCAR or XYZ. Structural relaxation itself and Anderson-disorder injection are not part of this input; for the disordered workflow you still need either a wrapper around rsatb::calc::apply_anderson_disorder or an externally generated disordered Hamiltonian read through an 'lcao'/'tb_file' model.

structure._comment: Replace with your relaxed moire cell. The tiling is the paper's transport supercell; drop it to [1, 1, 1] to work on the moire cell itself. Coordinates are used exactly as written -- nothing is wrapped or reordered -- so the tiled cell is the one you would get from ASE's repeat.

model._comment: The paper's parameters: Vpp_pi^0 = -2.7 eV, Vpp_sigma^0 = 0.3675 eV, q_pi/a0 = q_sigma/d0 = 22.18 nm^-1, a0 = 0.1439 nm, d0 = 0.33 nm, rc = 0.614 nm, lambda_c = 0.0265 nm. RSATB needs a finite graph cutoff, so the smooth Fermi cutoff is tabulated out to rc + 8 lambda_c = 8.26 A, where the residual tail is already negligible. The two files carry the closed form in their headers.

run._comment: No overlap, so the basis is orthogonal and velocity and position come for free -- which is what makes the MSD and the quantum metric available. MSD is defined from the Gamma-point wavepacket evolution, which is also the real-space supercell picture the paper works in. Fixed bounds skip the PRIMME estimate: on a cell this size that is both faster and more robust. Raise npar only if you add k-points; every rank must own at least one atom.
